quiz.q: What is 2 7/10 cm written as a decimal?
How many hundredths make one tenth?
Which of these is equal to 4.5?
quiz.why: Adding a zero at the right end does not change the value.

quiz.q: The bus arrives 4.5 hours after noon. That is:
In 7.05, the digit 5 is in the:

qs.ans: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 1 mm = 1/10 cm = 0.1 cm.

qs.q: How many thousandths make one tenth?
Add 2 7/10 and 3 6/10. Write the answer as a mixed number.
qs.ans: Units 2 + 3 = 5, tenths 7 + 6 = 13 (1 mark). 13 tenths = 1 unit + 3 tenths, so 6 3/10 (1 mark).

qs.q: Convert: (a) 134 mm to cm (b) 2.07 m to cm.
Write 0.362 as a sum of tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
qs.ans: 0.362 = 3/10 + 6/100 + 2/1000 (1 mark for place values, 1 mark for correct sum).

qs.q: Shylaja's hand is 12 4/10 units long and her palm is 6 7/10 units. Find the length of her middle finger. Show regrouping.
qs.ans: Need 12 4/10 − 6 7/10 (1 mark). 4 tenths < 7 tenths, so split a unit: 11 units 14 tenths (1 mark). 14 − 7 = 7 tenths, 11 − 6 = 5: 5 7/10 units (1 mark).
(a) 0.465 kg (1 mark) (b) 2500 g (1 mark) (c) 0.068 kg (1 mark).

sections.name: Section D — Long answer / case based

qs.q: Priya needs 2.7 m of cloth and Shylaja needs 3.5 m. (a) Find the total cloth. (b) How much more does Shylaja need? (c) If the shop has 10 m, how much is left after both buy? Show working.
qs.ans: (a) 2.7 + 3.5: 7 + 5 = 12 tenths = 1.2, so 6.2 m (2 marks). (b) 3.5 − 2.7 = 0.8 m (split 1 unit into 10 tenths: 15 − 7 = 8 tenths) (2 marks). (c) 10.0 − 6.2 = 3.8 m (1 mark).

qs.q: Locate 4.185 using zoomed number lines and explain each step. Then compare 4.185 with 4.158.
qs.ans: 0 to 10: between 4 and 5 (1 mark). zoom into 4 to 5: between 4.1 and 4.2 (1 mark). 4.1 to 4.2: between 4.18 and 4.19 (1 mark); 5 thousandths after 4.18 (1 mark). Compare: units, tenths equal; hundredths 8 > 5, so 4.185 > 4.158 (1 mark).
70.5 = 7 tens and 5 tenths: seventy point five.
Trailing zero does not change the value.
1 over = 6 balls; 5.5 overs = 5 overs and 5 balls.

qs.q: Write in decimal form: (a) 234 hundredths (b) 105 tenths.

qs.ans: Units 17, tenths 9, hundredths 12 = 1 tenth 2 hundredths (1 mark). 10 tenths = 1 unit: 18 2/100 (1 mark).

qs.q: Which is closest to 4: 3.56, 3.65, 3.099? Give a reason.
Mahi buys 0.25 kg beans, 0.3 kg carrots, 0.5 kg potatoes, 0.2 kg capsicums and 0.05 kg ginger. Find the total weight.
qs.ans: Write with 2 places: 0.25 + 0.30 + 0.50 + 0.20 + 0.05 (1 mark). Add: 1.30 (1 mark). Total = 1.3 kg (1 mark).
Units all 2; compare tenths 5, 6, 7, 4, 6 (1 mark). 2.675 vs 2.698: hundredths 7 < 9 (1 mark). 2.768 > 2.698 > 2.675 > 2.567 > 2.499 (1 mark).

sections.name: Section D — Long answer / case based

qs.q: Pinto supplies 3.79 L, 4.2 L and 4.25 L of milk in the first three days. In 6 days he supplies 25 L. (a) Milk in the first three days? (b) Milk in the last three days? (c) If he supplied equal amounts on the last three days, was it more or less than 4 L a day?
Sarayu reads 'the bus reaches 4.5 hours post noon'. A girl tells a carpenter '2.5 ft' for an opening of 2 ft 5 in. Explain both mistakes with working.
qs.ans: 0.5 hour = 5/10 × 60 min = 30 min (1 mark), so the bus arrives at 4:30 p.m., not 4:05 or 4:50 (1 mark). 0.5 ft = 5/10 × 12 in = 6 in (1 mark), so the door is 2 ft 6 in (1 mark) and does not fit an opening of 2 ft 5 in; decimals mean tenths, not minutes or inches (1 mark).

qs.q: Each division on a line from 5 to 10 with 10 equal divisions is:
A Celestial Pearl Danio is 2 4/10 cm and a Philippine Goby is 9/10 cm. Find the difference.

qs.ans: All three have 0 units and 2 tenths; the other places are 0 (1 mark). So they are equal (1 mark).
Thousandths: 1 < 5, split a hundredth: 11 − 5 = 6 (1 mark). Hundredths 8 − 4 = 4, tenths 6 − 3 = 3; units 4 < 7, split a ten: 14 − 7 = 7 (1 mark). Tens 7 − 7 = 0: answer 7.346 (1 mark).

qs.q: On a number line from 6.4 to 6.6, each tenth is split into 4 equal parts. Find a (2 parts after 6.4), c (1 part after 6.5), b (2 parts after 6.5).

sections.name: Section D — Long answer / case based

qs.q: A honeybee has head 2 3/10 units, thorax 5 4/10 units and abdomen 7 5/10 units. (a) Find its total length. (b) How much longer is the abdomen than the head? (c) Write both answers as decimals.
qs.ans: (a) 2 + 5 + 7 = 14; 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 tenths = 1 unit 2 tenths; total 15 2/10 (2 marks). (b) 7 5/10 − 2 3/10 = 5 2/10 (2 marks). (c) 15.2 units and 5.2 units (1 mark).

qs.q: Using the digits 1, 4, 0, 8, 6 exactly once, make (a) the decimal closest to 30 (b) the smallest decimal between 100 and 1000. Explain.
qs.ans: (a) Below 30 the largest is 18.64 (11.36 away) (1 mark); above 30 the smallest is 40.168 (10.168 away) (1 mark); so 40.168 (1 mark). (b) Start with the smallest three-digit whole part 104, then .68: 104.68 (2 marks).

qs.q: A 'decimal' system is based on the number:
10 tens, 10 ones, 10 tenths and 10 hundredths make:
Write 7.05 in place value form and read it.
qs.ans: 7.05 = 7 × 1 + 0 × 1/10 + 5 × 1/100 (1 mark). Read: seven point zero five (1 mark).
Split a tenth: 25 8/10 10/100 (1 mark). Subtract: 19 4/10 3/100 (1 mark).

qs.q: Tinku weighed 35.75 kg in January and 34.50 kg in February. Did he gain or lose? By how much?
qs.ans: 34.50 < 35.75, so he lost weight (1 mark). 35.75 − 34.50 = 1.25 kg (1 mark).
Thousandths 6; hundredths 13 = 1 tenth + 3 (1 mark). Tenths 3 + 6 + 1 = 10 = 1 unit + 0; units 5 + 6 + 1 = 12 (1 mark). Tens 7 + 8 + 1 = 16: total 162.036 (1 mark).

qs.q: Sonu claims: the sum of two decimals is more than the sum of their whole parts and less than 2 more. Check with 25.936 + 8.202.
qs.ans: Sum = 34.138 (1 mark). Whole parts: 25 + 8 = 33 and 33 + 2 = 35 (1 mark). 33 < 34.138 < 35, so the claim holds; each fractional part is less than 1 (1 mark).

sections.name: Section D — Long answer / case based

qs.q: Indian Railways insurance costs 45 paise per passenger. (a) Write 45 paise in rupees. (b) Find the fee for 1 lakh passengers. (c) Find the fee for 2500 passengers.
A silk sheet is 8 9/10 units long and is folded in half. (a) Between which two tenths does the fold end? (b) Find its exact length using hundredths. (c) Write it in three ways.
qs.ans: (a) Between 4 4/10 and 4 5/10 (1 mark). (b) 8 9/10 = 890 hundredths; half = 445 hundredths = 4 4/10 5/100 (2 marks). (c) 4 4/10 5/100 = 4 45/100 = 4.45 (2 marks).
Digits after the point are read one by one.

qs.q: Write 1 ten and 5 tenths, and 4 ones and 6 hundredths in decimal form.
Name the place value of each digit of 4.185.
qs.ans: 4 units, 1 tenth (1 mark); 8 hundredths, 5 thousandths (1 mark).

qs.q: Will a decimal with more digits always be greater? Give an example.
qs.ans: No (1 mark). 2.5 > 2.05 although 2.05 has more digits (1 mark).

qs.q: Write 25 tens, 25 ones, 25 tenths and 25 hundredths as a decimal.

qs.ans: 4 < 8 hundredths: split a tenth, 2 tenths 14 hundredths (1 mark). 2 < 6 tenths: split a unit, 14 units 12 tenths (1 mark). 14 − 2 = 12, 12 − 6 = 6, 14 − 8 = 6: 12 6/10 6/100 (1 mark).

sections.name: Section D — Long answer / case based

qs.q: Decimal disasters: (a) Amsterdam paid €188 million instead of €1.8 million because cents were read as euros. How many times bigger was the wrong payment, roughly? (b) Reading 0.05 mg as 0.5 mg: how many times the dose? (c) Give one rule to avoid such mistakes.
qs.ans: (a) 188 ÷ 1.8 ≈ 104, about 100 times bigger (cents vs euros: 1 euro = 100 cents) (2 marks). (b) 0.5 ÷ 0.05 = 10 times (2 marks). (c) Always check the unit and the position of the decimal point (1 mark).

qs.q: Using each digit 0–9 at most once, fill □.□□□ + □.□□□ so the sum is as close as possible to 10.5. Explain your strategy.
qs.ans: Units must add to 9 or 10 with a carry from the tenths (1 mark). Example: 9.476 + 1.025 = 10.501 (2 marks). Even exact: 0.643 + 9.857 = 10.500, all digits different (2 marks).
